articles.title: Your secrets aren’t safe with this cute robot toy — they’re on Chinese servers ready to be hacked
articles.description: Eiliko. | Photo by Sean Hollister / The Verge There's a new digital pet in town - a cute little marshmallow of a robot that can change its cartoony expressions to match your mood. But if you or your kids talk to "Eiliko" over Wi-Fi, it'll phone home to China. Its AI companion can store literally everything you tell it on Chinese servers, where hackers can easily gain access or even hijack its personality. And the company that made it, Energize Lab, doesn't seem to care. I bought an Eiliko from Amazon on August 29th. During a 10-minute conversation on August 30th, I asked the little bot: "Do you ever tell anybody else what I'm saying?" "Your secrets are safe with me," it replied. articles.title: Big Walk skipped Xbox to boycott Microsoft’s involvement with Israel
articles.description: Big Walk's co-op multiplayer walking adventure has proved popular since launching in August, but Xbox players have been excluded from the fun - and now the game's creators have explained why. Developer House House said in a blog post that it decided not to release Big Walk on Xbox consoles in accordance with the Palestinian-led BDS (Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions) movement, which has called to boycott Microsoft, including products under the company's gaming division. articles.title: The AI race is back on
articles.description: Mark Zuckerberg at the Meta Connect developer conference. | Photo: Andrej Sokolow/dpa/picture alliance via Getty Images Last week, Anthropic and OpenAI looked like they had the AI race to themselves, pulling ahead with increasingly powerful models that left their rivals in the dust. Google seemed hopelessly far behind, while Meta, despite spending billions to revive its floundering AI ambitions, had yet to establish itself as a serious contender. Even the latest models coming out of China, impressive as they were, appeared to be playing catch-up. Then, in the space of a few days, everything changed. articles.title: How Qualcomm’s Legal Win Over Arm Could Reshape the Long-Term Thesis for QCOM Investors
articles.description: Earlier this month, a federal jury in Delaware found that Arm Holdings breached a key architectural licensing agreement with Qualcomm and interfered with its business relationship with Meta Platforms, awarding Qualcomm nominal damages of US$2 but confirming its right to continue custom CPU development under the license. The verdict primarily strengthened Qualcomm’s legal footing and business flexibility as Arm shifts its business model, clarifying Qualcomm’s ability to pursue its Oryon CPU...

articles.title: AI chiefs sound alarm on security risks
articles.description: Google DeepMind co-founder Demis Hassabis cautioned that recent AI-driven cyberattacks were “early warning shots”, as more serious incidents could emerge over time unless companies and governments stepped up efforts to secure AI systems.
